newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Five killed as sprawling Nigerian market burns.
newsitem.headline: Five killed as sprawling Nigerian market burns.

text.p: Five people died when Onitsha market in eastern Nigeria, reputed to be the biggest in West Africa, burnt down, local newspapers reported on Wednesday.
Vanguard newspaper said fire broke out at dawn on Tuesday and traders watched helplessly as their wares went up in flames.

It said the local military administrator, Group Captain Rufai Garba, went to the scene to pay a sympathy visit but his convoy of limousines was pelted with stones by irate traders angry that the fire service was unable to put out the flames.
The cause of the fire was not immediately known.

The Onitsha market, situated on the bank of the River Niger, separating eastern Nigeria from the western part, spreads over a large area and displays all manner of items ranging from food to building materials.
It is the third fire incident there in 11 years.
